claim: In a 280-person CHI 2025 study, using LLMs (free-form, direct generation, or a reframing-theory structured method) did not improve problem frame quality.
quote: We found that using LLMs does not help improve the quality of problem frames.
title: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing
transfer: Do not assume an LLM frame step adds value; test a frame step against plain diverge at equal tokens, and keep it off by default.

claim: The same study found the gap between experienced and inexperienced designers widened and inexperienced designers reported lower agency with LLMs (summary of abstract, not verbatim).
title: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing
transfer: LLM help is uneven: gains go to those who already frame well. A frame step may help only when the model already has a good prior; log per-item variance.

claim: LLM design agents fixate on existing paradigms; a separate metacognitive co-regulation agent beat self-regulation, which beat a plain loop, on one battery-pack design problem without much more compute (preprint).
title: Supervising Ralph Wiggum: Exploring a Metacognitive Co-Regulation Agentic AI Loop for Engineering Design
transfer: External stuck-check call on open routes only. Single task, so treat as a hypothesis, not a result.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction in reasoning, without external feedback, often fails and sometimes lowers performance.
quote: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance even degrades after self-correction.
authors: Huang, Chen, Mishra, Zheng, Yu, Song, Zhou
title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
transfer: Schon-style reflection must be triggered by a real check output (test, example mismatch), not by the model re-reading itself.

claim: A critical survey found no prior work shows successful self-correction using feedback from prompted LLMs, except on tasks unusually suited to it; self-correction works when reliable external feedback exists.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
transfer: Reframe or revise only when an external signal exists. Evaluators that are the same prompted model do not count as external.

claim: Chain-of-thought can reduce accuracy on tasks where deliberation also hurts humans; up to 36.3% absolute drop for o1-preview versus GPT-4o in three of six tasks, mixed in the rest.
quote: six representative tasks from the psychological literature where deliberation hurts performance in humans
authors: Liu, Geng, Wu, Sucholutsky, Lombrozo, Griffiths
title: Mind Your Step (by Step): Chain-of-Thought can Reduce Performance on Tasks where Thinking Makes Humans Worse
transfer: Router rule: do not force explicit deliberation or reframing on tasks where the first intuitive answer is usually right. Matches our ARC and word-puzzle losses.

claim: Making reasoning models think longer can lower accuracy (inverse scaling in test-time compute), with five failure modes including distraction by irrelevant information in Claude models.
quote: Claude models become increasingly distracted by irrelevant information.
authors: Gema, Hagele, Chen, Arditi, et al.
title: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
transfer: Cap reframing cycles and total thinking per call; add a stop rule when the answer is already stable.

claim: o1-like models spend large compute on simple problems with minimal benefit (overthinking).
quote: excessive computational resources are allocated for simple problems with minimal benefit
authors: Chen, Xu, Liang, He, et al.
title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
transfer: A cheap well-posed vs open-ended router before any frame step; skip frames on easy items.

claim: Access to GenAI ideas raised individual creativity of writers but made their stories more similar to each other (lower collective diversity).
quote: GenAI-enabled stories are more similar to each other than stories by humans alone
title: Generative artificial intelligence enhances creativity but reduces the diversity of novel content
venue: arXiv 2312.00506 (journal version Science Advances 2024, not opened)
transfer: Same-model samples converge. Frames from one model may also converge; measure distinct frames, not just distinct answers.

claim: The earlier brief's 'curated reasoning improved design quality' is a human-LLM interface study (DesignerlyLoop, 20 designers), not evidence that an agent procedure helps.
quote: significantly improves design quality and creativity
title: DesignerlyLoop: Forming Design Intent through Curated Reasoning for Human-LLM Alignment
transfer: none. Downgrade in the synthesis: the benefit came from humans editing the reasoning, which a program-run schema lacks.

claim: AI assistants show sycophancy across tasks, and humans and preference models sometimes prefer sycophantic answers over correct ones; relevant to a reflection or critic call that tends to agree with the draft.
quote: five state-of-the-art AI assistants consistently exhibit sycophancy
authors: Sharma, Tong, Korbak, Duvenaud, Askell, et al.
title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
transfer: A critic or co-regulator call should be given the draft without the author's framing, and asked for a specific failure, so it cannot just approve.

claim: Dorst and Cross co-evolution model came from protocols of nine experienced designers on one task; small sample.
title: Creativity in the design process: co-evolution of problem-solution
transfer: Treat the bridge step as a hypothesis with a cap; test its value by how often it changes the winner. Earlier brief marked this as checked by abstract; I did not reopen it.

claim: Kruger and Cross found four design strategies in nine designers and no simple link between strategy and solution quality; solution-driven designers did not do worse (as reported in the earlier brief).
title: Solution driven versus problem driven design: strategies and outcomes
transfer: No rule 'analyse problem first'. My fetch of the URL returned 403, so this is unverified by me.

claim: A later conference paper (Kokotovich, IASDR 2015) argues co-evolution is read too loosely in the literature and proposes mapping the problem space; I could not read the PDF text, so the content is from the earlier brief only.
title: IASDR 2015 paper on interpretation of the co-evolution model

claim: Jansson and Smith 1991 showed designers given an example copy its flaws; Sio, Kotovsky and Cagan 2015 review the example effects and report mixed results (earlier brief: a review, not a verified meta-analysis).
title: Design fixation (1991); Fixation or inspiration? review of examples on design processes (2015)
transfer: Examples can inspire or fixate, so lessons from memory should be tested shown after first generation versus before. ScienceDirect returned 403; unverified by me.

claim: The earlier brief claim that Zhang et al. and ICCC 2026 paper 78 support LLM reframing is weak: ICCC paper rated 27 outputs by 7 students, and I could not read either PDF text.
title: LLM reframing under three prompting strategies (as titled in earlier brief)
transfer: none. Do not cite as support.
